title: Ibovespa Rises on Lower Oil Prices
body: The Ibovespa rose 0.7% on Monday to close at 186,596, rebounding after ending the previous week in negative territory amid weaker international oil prices. Crude declined on expectations of diplomatic progress between the US and Iran. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is expected to attend the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week, and US President Donald Trump signaled he would be open to meeting him. Bond yields eased as the pause in the oil rally tempered concerns over energy-driven inflation, supporting credit-sensitive stocks. Financials advanced, with Itaú gaining 1.8% and Bradesco up 0.9%. Utilities also moved higher, led by Axia, which climbed 2.5%. In the local macroeconomic outlook, the financial market trimmed its 2026 Selic rate forecast from 13.75% to 13.50%, while slightly raising its 2026 inflation projection from 4.90% to 4.92%, according to the Brazilian Central Bank's Focus Bulletin. title: TSX Rises as Banks Gain
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index advanced 0.6% on Monday to close at 36,009, driven by strength in major bank stocks. Oil prices retreated amid optimism over potential diplomatic progress between the United States and Iran. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is expected to attend the UN General Assembly this week, and US President Donald Trump indicated he would be open to meeting him. Bond yields eased as the pullback in oil prices tempered inflation concerns, providing support to credit-sensitive sectors. Financials outperformed, with notable gains among the major banks: Royal Bank of Canada (+1.8%), TD Bank (+1.5%), Bank of Montreal (+1.8%), Bank of Nova Scotia (+1.7%), and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (+1.4%). Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem reiterated that monetary policy cannot reverse the effects of tariffs or directly influence gasoline prices, but emphasized that the central bank must evaluate the persistence of these shocks and their implications for inflation and economic growth. In contrast, energy stocks weakened, with Canadian Natural Resources down 2.2% and Suncor off 2.7%. Mining shares also declined, with Wheaton Precious Metals (WPM) slipping 1.6%. title: Oil Extends Losses on US-Iran Diplomacy Hopes
body: Crude oil fell below $95.50 a barrel on Monday, extending losses into a fourth consecutive session after reports that US President Trump had decided, for now, against bombing Yemen and signaled openness to diplomacy with Iran. Trump was said to have rejected Saudi Arabia's calls for strikes against the Houthis and indicated he would probably be willing to meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during this week's UN General Assembly in New York. At the same time, Middle Eastern crude exports have remained resilient despite Saudi Arabia's decision to shut its East–West pipeline following recent attacks. Over the past six days, Saudi Arabia has shipped about 2.9 million barrels per day through the Strait of Hormuz. Satellite imagery over the weekend showed supertankers with a combined capacity of 14 million barrels berthed at Saudi export terminals in the Gulf—the largest tanker presence recorded since at least June. Nonetheless, overall traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has continued to decline. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: US Stocks Rise on Easing Yields and Tech Gains
body: US stock indices closed higher on Monday as Treasury yields retreated, briefly easing worries about a challenging macroeconomic backdrop and fueling a renewed rally in technology shares. The S&P 500 advanced 1.5%, the Nasdaq climbed 2.3% to a record close of 27,122, and the Dow gained 366 points. President Trump said he would be open to meeting his Iranian counterpart, Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. At the same time, observed Saudi oil loadings from within the Persian Gulf jumped over the weekend. Crude oil and refined product prices continued to retreat from their monthly peaks, easing recent pressure on the bond market. Lower funding costs improved the outlook for AI hyperscalers to keep issuing debt at record levels, bolstering chipmakers and AI infrastructure stocks. Additional optimism over future chip demand was driven by signs of early success for Meta's (+11.4%) new AI agent. AMD surged 9.9%, closing above a $1 trillion market capitalization for the first time, while Intel rallied 12.1%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Paraguay Holds Key Interest Rate at 5.50%
body: Paraguay's central bank left its policy rate unchanged at 5.50% at its September 2026 meeting. The bank stated that economic activity continues to perform well and remains consistent with its projected 4.5% growth for 2026. Annual inflation is still low, largely reflecting the behavior of goods prices, which rose 0.4%, driven mainly by non-energy goods. By contrast, inflation in services and rents is hovering around 3.5%. The bank projects year-end inflation at 3.3%, with a gradual convergence toward the target over the monetary policy horizon. Inflation expectations also remain anchored at the target. The external environment, however, continues to face risks. These include volatility in international petroleum product prices and uncertainty stemming from the conflict in the Middle East, particularly its potential impact on supply conditions and energy prices. In addition, market participants expect at least one more increase in the federal funds rate before the end of the year. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com
